title: The great Hampton band and Herbie Fields's Fort Dix background
summary: Cobb lists key members of Hampton's best band, including Milton Buckner, Charlie Harris and Sinclair, then explains who Herbie Fields was before joining.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: You better know it. See, that's what made the band get sick and people started to going away, you know, because at that time we had a hell of a band. We had two bass players. Milton Buckner on piano, Charlie Harris, who left Hampton, went with Nat King Cole out of Baltimore, Maryland, and stayed with Nat until he died. Sinclair, the other bass player was on that band. He was killed in an accident by getting panicky and jumped out of the car before the accident occurred. He saw it coming up and jumped out, and he's the only one got killed.
That was one of the finest bands of all time out of the fiye years I was there, that band we had. Herbert Field was on that band.
I'll tell you how he got there.
They had -- at MCA they had -- he was
going around. He was the bandleader from the Army Camp down (inaudible) Jersey, Sergeant Herbert Fields coming from what's that camp in Jersey, and he broadcast on Sundays. Oh --

Fort Dix, that's it. And he come out of the army, and he was running around with horns under his arms, jamming all over New York and upsetting everybody, and MCA had a guy by the name of Johnny Boswell that they were billing, and they sent a man out to (inaudible) Herbert Field up and sign him up. And they did. They signed him up to get him out of (inaudible) because he was running two, three around there, playing all them horns and exciting people.
